_comment: Every development example where a verified reference program disagreed
with nuScenes-QA, read one by one and placed in a category. Nothing here
changes a reference answer and nothing is dropped from the manifest: the
point of the category is to say which of the three possible faults it is
-- the program, the executor, or a disagreement between the executor's
conventions and the dataset's -- before any model is blamed for it.
Produced against manifest version 1, records_dev.jsonl of the run with

dataset_does_not_presuppose_uniqueness.what: A one-hop question whose definite reference matches many objects. The executor refuses; nuScenes-QA answers anyway.
dataset_does_not_presuppose_uniqueness.whose_fault: neither: a semantic difference between the executor and the dataset
dataset_does_not_presuppose_uniqueness.evidence: 'the not standing pedestrian' matches 22 pedestrians in that sample, and the gold answer is still 'yes'. The dataset's one-hop templates appear to read the reference existentially -- is there SOME such object with the property -- rather than as a definite description.
dataset_does_not_presuppose_uniqueness.action: left as a refusal. Reading it existentially would turn a question we cannot resolve into a disjunction over 22 anchors, which is a different question and would score by luck. Recorded as a known cost of the uniqueness requirement; it is charged against the executed system in the comparison, not excused.

diagonal_sector_boundary.what: A directional count that disagrees, always on a diagonal sector (front_left, front_right, back_left, back_right), never on a plain front or back.
diagonal_sector_boundary.whose_fault: the spatial convention, shared by both systems
diagonal_sector_boundary.evidence: On the development split the executor agrees with 50/50 non-directional questions, 17/18 axial ones (front, back) and 24/32 diagonal ones; front_left alone is 5/10. The convention itself was checked against the gold answers rather than assumed: over the 68 ego-anchored directional questions of the manifest, uniform 60-degree sectors with no range limit score 76.5% exact, beating a mirrored y axis (72.1%), the six nuScenes camera fields of view (67.6%), 45-degree octants (61.8%) and overlapping quadrants (51.5%), and every maximum-range cut from 25 m to 60 m makes it worse. So the convention is the best-fitting of the five tested, and the residual sits on the diagonal boundaries.
diagonal_sector_boundary.action: not fitted away. Boundaries chosen to maximise agreement with the gold answers would be an executor tuned on the test signal, and the executed system -- which computes with those boundaries -- would gain from it far more than the direct system, which only reads them in prose. The uniform 60-degree reading of the published definition is kept, the residual is reported, and both systems are given the same convention so the mismatch cannot favour either.
